answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a refundable bond before it may bid, then slash that bond when an independently audited task reveals fabricated work or collusive identities. Auditors sample completed jobs and compare outputs against hidden tests, so copying a public answer is risky. A tide of cheap accounts no longer creates free influence: each Sybil ties up capital and must risk losing it. Quartz records can make bond history tamper-evident, though no ledger proves one human per account; the fable of perfect identity control is unnecessary when deception has a price.
